**Alter Domus Intelligence (ADI)**

ADI’s first use cases go live in October 2026, and the platform is now building toward a much broader product vision across the entire client and investor journey.
   

  

**About The Role**
 We are looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the
 **ADI Platform** 
 — the technical and product foundation on which every ADI squad builds. ADI is a micro front\\-end (MFE) architecture: a common shell (authentication, navigation, notifications, search, component library, home and admin pages) into which independent squads — Investor, Payments, Fund of Funds, Reporting and others — plug their surfaces. Without a well\\-owned, well\\-governed platform layer, those surfaces fragment, degrade, and slow down. This role exists to prevent that.
   

  

 You are not building features for end users directly — you are building
 **the product that enables every other product team**

At the same time, you own capabilities that are end\\-user facing and mission\\-critical: authentication and access control, the home experience, notifications, universal search, and the shared component library. You must hold the platform to the same rigour as any customer\\-facing product — with performance, availability, security and developer experience treated as first\\-class requirements.

* Act as the product authority for the platform, making the decisions that trade off between feature\\-squad needs and platform coherence.


**Developer Experience \\& Internal Product**
* Treat the other ADI squads as your primary customers — understand their dependency needs, pain points and roadmap commitments, and design the platform to enable them rather than constrain them.
* Own the golden\\-path developer experience: template projects, the shared NPM component library (Photon), CI/CD patterns, MFE composition standards, and deployment infrastructure — ensuring every squad has a well\\-lit path to building and shipping.
* Establish and govern the standards and contracts between the platform and squad microsites — import maps, API standards, component versioning, and token enrichment — so the platform can evolve without breaking consumers.
* Work alongside the other product managers to help their teams onboard to, and correctly consume, platform capabilities.


**Authentication, authorisation \\& multi\\-tenancy**
* Own the end\\-to\\-end authentication and authorisation product: integration with CIAM and GSP, role\\-based access control (RBAC), UI component\\-level authorisation patterns, token enrichment, and the multi\\-tenancy and client\\-isolation model.
* Define the access model clearly — who can see what, in which context, for which client or fund — and ensure it is implemented consistently across every squad’s surface.
* Own org context switching, user account management (/account), and the admin experience (/admin).


**Core Platform Experiences**
* Own the ADI home page — including the customisable widget framework (calendar views, user\\-based preferences) — and ensure it serves as a coherent, high\\-value landing experience for all user personas.
* Own universal search across ADI — defining scope, relevance, and the integration model with squad\\-specific content — in alignment with the AI\\-unified search strategy.
* Own the notifications engine — defining the notification taxonomy, routing logic, SLA and priority model, and the interfaces through which feature squads publish notifications — and partner with the squads (e.g. Fund of Funds, Payments) who consume it.
* Own the cross\\-team calendar service, the feature\\-flagging framework, and user\\-analytics instrumentation.


**Non\\-functional Requirements \\& Operational Readiness**
* Own platform\\-level non\\-functional requirements — performance, availability, scalability, security (including penetration testing), accessibility and observability — as first\\-class product requirements, not afterthoughts.
* Define the platform’s SLAs and the squad contracts that rely on them; ensure monitoring, logging, error handling, alerting and rollback capability are production\\-grade from day one.
* Own the global and regional deployment and caching strategy, and the CI/CD framework that all squads depend on.


**Building AI\\-Native — How We Work**
* Author Executable PRDs (xPRDs) — structured context repositories that combine natural\\-language intent, machine\\-actionable specification, complete business and technical context, edge cases, success metrics and acceptance criteria, and embedded governance guardrails.
* Build the first functional prototype yourself during ideation and discovery, using AI tooling to validate desirability (product\\-market fit with clients) and feasibility (with architects) in parallel — then hand a high\\-fidelity, context\\-rich prototype to engineering to curate and take to production quality.
* Own the non\\-functional requirements — performance, availability, scalability, security and accessibility — from day one, treating them as first\\-class product requirements rather than an afterthought.
* Work within an enhanced design\\-thinking approach with governance embedded from day one — ethical AI and user rights, privacy, security, risk and compliance, and audit/traceability — alongside explicit attention to data readiness (maturity, availability and quality).


**Quality \\& governance**
* Own platform quality, reliability and consistency governance — establishing the standards and review processes that prevent squad divergence from platform contracts.
* Embed security, privacy, accessibility (WCAG), and auditability into platform decisions from the outset.
* Own the API\\-standards governance framework across ADI — ensuring consistent, well\\-documented APIs across squads, aligned to OpenAPI/Swagger standards.


**Delivery \\& cross\\-functional**
* Act as product lead for the Platform squad; partner with engineering and architecture on delivery, and with every other squad PM to manage dependencies, prioritise shared roadmap items, and unblock delivery.
* Act as the interface between the platform and the ADI programme — representing platform capacity, constraints and roadmap in planning and senior\\-stakeholder forums.


**Essential**
**SKILLS \\& EXPERIENCE:**
* Proven senior product management experience delivering platform, infrastructure, or developer\\-experience products in a complex, multi\\-team technology environment — owning products whose primary customers are internal engineering teams.
* Deep understanding of micro front\\-end (MFE) architecture, front\\-end platform patterns, component libraries, and API design — sufficient to hold technical discussions with architects and make grounded product decisions.
